title: dotagents repository profile
description: Per-repository verification config. Lives here rather than in the product repo so product repos stay unmodified. Resolved by matching the git remote of the working directory.

match.description: How to recognise the repository this profile applies to.

remote.description: Substring, or list of substrings any of which matches, tested against `git remote get-url origin`. 'owner/repo' pins one owner; '/repo' follows the repository through forks and through both URL forms (https and ssh). A list is for a repository reachable under several names.

cwd.description: Directory relative to the repo root where checks run. Omit to run at the root.

spec_system.description: How this repository records intent before code exists. A per-repository fact that the toolkit had nowhere to put: the routing lived as a parenthetical in README.md, which is never loaded at runtime, so nothing ever read it. Omit for a repository that records intent nowhere -- and then say so in the report rather than inventing a location for it.

kind.description: openspec: the repository has openspec/{specs,changes} and one change is a DIRECTORY -- proposal, design, tasks, plus spec deltas per capability. plans: one Markdown plan per change, the shape upstream writing-plans produces. none: intent is not recorded on disk here, so do not invent a convention for it.

root.description: Directory holding the artifacts, relative to the repo root. 'openspec' for openspec; for plans, wherever the plan files live.

rules.description: File carrying the repository's OWN authoring rules, to be read before writing or reviewing anything here. For openspec that is 'openspec/config.yaml', which states the required headings, the normative vocabulary, and that a MODIFIED requirement is restated whole. Reviewing against generic dimensions while the repository has written its own down is the failure this field exists to stop.

validate.description: Command that mechanically checks one change, as ARGV -- not a shell string. One element per argument; the element that is exactly '<id>' is replaced by the change id. Example: ["pnpm", "openspec", "validate", "<id>", "--strict"]. Argv rather than a string on purpose: a profile cannot then smuggle a pipeline, a ';', or a substitution past a reader, and the change id cannot escape into the command because it is its own element. An argv beginning with a shell (sh/bash/zsh) or containing '-c' defeats that and must be refused by whatever runs it. Run it and report its output as evidence BEFORE judging -- a spec whose validity is machine-checkable must not be reviewed by reading alone, which is the rule da-verify applies to code, applied to intent.

max_attempts.description: Consecutive failures of the same check before the gate stops blocking and records that it gave up. Default 3. Blocking forever is not a guardrail: the escalation it used to print told the agent to run /clear, which nothing running unattended can do. Giving up is recorded in a VERDICT file so it cannot be mistaken for a pass.

timeout_total.description: Seconds the gate may spend on all checks in one turn end. Default 300. Not decoration: N checks times their individual timeouts can exceed the agent harness's own hook timeout, and being killed by THAT is the one failure the gate cannot observe -- the process exits with neither 0 nor 2, which is non-blocking, so a slow suite becomes a silent pass. The hook entry in templates/ declares a timeout strictly larger than this so our clock is always the one that fires. When the budget runs out the gate reports which checks it never started and blocks: an unrun gating check is not a pass.

forbidden.description: Command substrings that must never be executed by an agent in this repository. Deploys, destroys, and anything that touches a live environment.

allOf.$comment: An unexplained request to run something by hand reads as arbitrary and gets ignored, so the schema requires the reason rather than a document asking for it.
scope:changed narrows a command to the changed files, which only means anything if the command has somewhere to put them.

cmd.description: Shell command. `{files}` is replaced with the changed files when scope is 'changed'.

gate.description: True if failing this check must block completion.

agent_may_run.description: False when the repository forbids the agent from running it, or when it needs resources or credentials the agent should not consume. Interactively the agent must ask the user to run it and wait for the output. UNATTENDED (scripts/loop.sh) there is nobody to ask and no number of rounds can satisfy it, so the driver records the check as deferred and proceeds -- naming it in the ledger, in the run's closing message and in the PR body, because a deferred gate is no more green than a released one. That means CI is the gate for these checks: the prohibition is on RUNNING them, not on shipping them verified. If the repository's CI does not run it either, there is nowhere to defer to -- set gate:false deliberately, or add it to CI.

delegate_reason.description: Required when agent_may_run is false. Shown to the user so the request is not arbitrary.

scope.description: 'changed' narrows the command to files touched in the working tree.

timeout.description: Seconds this check may run before the gate kills it. Default 120. A timeout is treated as a malfunction of the gate rather than a finding about the code -- it blocks, and it is recorded as reason 'timeout' rather than 'red', because it says nothing about whether the code is correct. It counts toward max_attempts, or a genuinely hanging check would block every turn forever.

mutates.description: True when running this check can rewrite the working tree -- an auto-fixer such as lint:fix or format:fix. The gate still runs it, but a run that changes the tree blocks instead of reporting green: the hook has just modified the files the agent had decided it was done with, and in a loop the next iteration would read a tree it did not write. Nothing is reverted; the next turn passes once there is nothing left to fix. A gate that repairs things quietly is a gate whose green cannot be trusted.

when.description: Human-readable condition for conditional checks. Only meaningful when gate is false. NOT a predicate -- nothing reads it at runtime. The executed mechanisms are `paths` (whether the check runs) and `{files}` in `cmd` (what it runs on).

paths.description: WHETHER the check runs, orthogonal to `scope`, which is WHAT it runs on. Both together are normal and correct: "only when scripts/ changed, and then over everything" is `paths` plus `scope: all`. A schema rule forbidding that pair shipped here for one landing and was wrong -- it read `scope: all` as "always runs", which is not what scope means. Repo-root-relative prefixes or globs; a trailing /** is a prefix. The check runs only when at least one changed file matches. Omit to always run. ROOT-relative, not cwd-relative -- a profile with "cwd": "pkg" still writes "pkg/src/**"; getting that backwards matches nothing, which would skip the check every turn. Skips are named in `verify --json`'s `skipped` rather than vanishing, and if files changed that NO gating check claims, the gate BLOCKS with kind not_checked: unclaimed files are a hole in the profile, not a pass.
